title: Bowling Game with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a 3D bowling game using Three.js with particle effects.

## Scene Setup
- Use Three.js via CDN (r160+) with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls.
- Set up a perspective camera at position (0, 8, 18) looking toward (0, 0, -10).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Create a bowling lane: a long box (width 3, height 0.2, length 30) colored #C4A45A (wood tone), centered at (0, -0.1, -5).
- Add gutter walls on each side of the lane (thin boxes, dark gray).

## Bowling Ball
- Create a sphere (radius 0.4) colored dark blue (#1a1a8a) positioned at (0, 0.4, 10) — this is the starting position.
- The ball is the object the player launches.

## Bowling Pins
- Load the 'Lantern.glb' model using GLTFLoader. Use this model as bowling pins.
- Scale each lantern model to (0.3, 0.3, 0.3) so they serve as pin-sized objects.
- Arrange 10 pins in standard bowling triangle formation at z = -12:
  - Row 1 (front): 1 pin at (0, 0, -12)
  - Row 2: 2 pins at (-0.5, 0, -12.8) and (0.5, 0, -12.8)
  - Row 3: 3 pins at (-1, 0, -13.6), (0, 0, -13.6), (1, 0, -13.6)
  - Row 4: 4 pins at (-1.5, 0, -14.4), (-0.5, 0, -14.4), (0.5, 0, -14.4), (1.5, 0, -14.4)
- Each pin's y position should place it on top of the lane surface.

## Aiming & Launching
- Before launching, the player can aim using LEFT/RIGHT arrow keys to move the ball along the x-axis (clamped to -1.2 to 1.2).
- Press SPACEBAR to launch the ball. The ball moves forward (negative z) at a speed of 15 units/second.
- The ball can only be launched once per round. After launch, arrow keys are disabled.

## Collision & Pin Knockdown
- Implement simple collision detection: when the ball's position is within 0.6 units of a pin's position (distance in xz plane), that pin is 'knocked down'.
- When a pin is knocked down: rotate it 90 degrees on the x-axis (lay it flat), move it slightly, and mark it as knocked.
- Track the number of pins knocked down.

## Particle Effects
- When a pin is knocked down, spawn a burst of 20 small particles (small spheres or points, yellow/orange colored) at the pin's position.
- Particles should spread outward in random directions and fade out (reduce opacity) over 1 second, then be removed.
- Use a simple particle system: an array of small meshes with velocity and lifetime.

## Reset
- Add a 'Reset' button (DOM button, id='resetBtn') that resets the ball to starting position, stands all pins back up, resets score, and clears particles.

## HUD / UI
- Display current score (pins knocked down) in a div with id='scoreDisplay' showing text like 'Score: 0'.
- Display game state in a div with id='gameStatus' showing 'Aiming' before launch, 'Rolling' during ball travel, and 'Finished' when ball passes z = -18 or all pins are down.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
  - ballPosition: {x, y, z} — current ball position
  - ballLaunched: boolean — whether ball has been launched
  - pinsDown: number — count of knocked down pins (0-10)
  - totalPins: number — always 10
  - gamePhase: string — 'aiming', 'rolling', or 'finished'
  - particlesActive: number — current number of active particles in the scene
  - pinsLoaded: boolean — true once all 10 lantern models are loaded and placed

## Animation Loop
- Use requestAnimationFrame. Update ball position each frame if launched. Check collisions. Update particles. Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.
physics_constraints: Ball moves in straight line along z-axis at constant speed. Pin knockdown triggered by proximity collision (distance < 0.6). Ball x-position clamped to [-1.2, 1.2]. Particles obey simple linear motion with gravity-like downward acceleration and 1-second lifetime.
